title: High-Performance Structured Logging for AI
description: Implement zero-allocation structured logging with LoggerMessage source generators, session correlation scopes, and PII masking in C#.

data.text: The Need for Structured Logging in AI Systems

Logging raw string messages (e.g. _logger.LogInformation($"User {userId} asked: {prompt}")) is an anti-pattern. String interpolation causes unnecessary heap allocations, slows down throughput, and generates unstructured text that search engines cannot query or index efficiently. In production AI systems, structured logging captures properties as discrete key-value pairs (TenantId, ModelId, PromptTokens, LatencyMs), enabling fast filtering and aggregations across millions of log entries.
C# compile-time source generators ([LoggerMessage]) eliminate boxing, string formatting, and parsing overhead, yielding the fastest possible logging implementation in .NET.

data.title: High-Performance AI Logger Generator in C#
data.content: Defines compile-time generated logging methods for AI operations:
data.code:
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;

public static partial class AiLogEvents
{
    [LoggerMessage(
        EventId = 2001,
        Level = LogLevel.Information,
        Message = "Completed AI completion for model {Model} in {ElapsedMs}ms. Tokens: {PromptTokens} prompt, {CompletionTokens} completion.")]
    public static partial void LogAiCompletionSuccess(
        this ILogger logger,
        string model,
        long elapsedMs,
        int promptTokens,
        int completionTokens);

    [LoggerMessage(
        EventId = 2002,
        Level = LogLevel.Warning,
        Message = "Rate limit 429 throttled for model {Model}. Retry attempt {RetryAttempt} after {RetryDelaySeconds}s.")]
    public static partial void LogAiRateLimitThrottled(
        this ILogger logger,
        string model,
        int retryAttempt,
        double retryDelaySeconds);

    [LoggerMessage(
        EventId = 2003,
        Level = LogLevel.Error,
        Message = "Tool execution '{ToolName}' threw exception on tenant {TenantId}.")]
    public static partial void LogToolExecutionFailure(
        this ILogger logger,
        string toolName,
        string tenantId,
        Exception ex);
}

data.text: Correlating Multi-Turn Conversations with Logging Scopes

In complex agentic or conversational systems, an individual user request might trigger retrieval, five tool invocations, and two LLM calls. Using _logger.BeginScope() attaches correlation properties (SessionId, TurnId, TenantId) to every log statement executed within that async execution context.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Never use string interpolation in logging: use structured key-value property templates
Use [LoggerMessage] compile-time source generators for zero-allocation performance
Capture essential AI metrics: ModelId, PromptTokens, CompletionTokens, LatencyMs
Wrap multi-turn sessions in ILogger.BeginScope() to correlate logs across tools and LLM calls
Sanitize logs to prevent customer PII or raw API keys from entering log analytics sinks
data.takeaway: Structured logging turns noisy text files into queryable telemetry databases. Leveraging source generators and logging scopes provides high-throughput, correlated diagnostics across your AI stack.
